title: Mammal sighting declines in Everglades National Park since pythons arrived

source.name: Severe mammal declines coincide with proliferation of invasive Burmese pythons in Everglades National Park

notes: USGS-backed road-survey study (nearly 39,000 miles driven, 2003-2011, compared against 1996-1997 baseline surveys) found raccoon observations down 99.3%, opossum 98.9%, white-tailed deer 94.1% and bobcat 87.5% in the areas of the park where pythons have been established longest. Marsh rabbits, cottontail rabbits and foxes were not observed at all during the later surveys.
